newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen mayor pledges support for Vulkan yard.
newsitem.headline: Bremen mayor pledges support for Vulkan yard.

text.p: The mayor of the city-state of Bremen on Wednesday pledged his support to secure millions of marks needed to keep open the Bremer Vulkan shipyard, the area's biggest employer.

Henning Scherf, the mayor of Bremen, told some 1,000 shipyard workers he would lobby the government to guarantee a 42 million mark loan, made available by Germany's KfW, the Federal Reconstruction Corporation.
The loan is needed to keep the yard, once the flagship of Germany's then-biggest shipbuilder Bremer Vulkan Verbund AG which declared bankruptcy in May, in business.
Scherf said a decision should be reached on the matter today.
On Tuesday the group's court appointed administrator Jobst Wellensiek painted a dire picture that this loan is the linchpin for the yard's survival.
"Closing the plant cannot be ruled out, but to take a decision on it today would not be right," Wellensiek said on Tuesday.

Bremer Vulkan collapsed in May after posting huge losses and being accused of having misappropriated hundreds of millions of marks in state aid cleared by the European Union for use in eastern Germany.
The shipyards were one of the region's largest employers and their collapse has sent the unemployment rate, already above the national average, sharply higher.
